narrative:
The model determined that you have a 37% chance of representing a bad credit risk. Because this probability exceeded the bank's acceptance threshold, your loan application was denied.

The three factors that most strongly shaped this outcome were the status of your checking account, the purpose of the loan, and the requested loan duration. Your checking account being in negative balance (<0 DM) was the single biggest reason for the denial. Among approved applicants, only 12.6% have a negative account, while 59% have no checking account at all. This status strongly pushed the prediction toward bad credit risk.

The purpose of the loan (to buy a radio or TV) worked in your favor and pulled the prediction back toward approval. This is a relatively common and lower-risk purpose compared with some other categories. Similarly, requesting only a 12-month loan was viewed positively. Approved loans in the dataset average 19 months, so your shorter duration helped reduce the risk score.

Unfortunately, the negative effect of your checking-account status outweighed these positive signals. 

You should focus on bringing your checking account into positive territory or building a buffer of savings before reapplying. This single change would likely have the largest impact on improving your chances with future applications.
